concepts.name: Autoregressive Chunking with Overlap
concepts.summary: The dominant way to push Wan (pretrained ~5 s / 81 frames = T_max) past its ceiling in ComfyUI: generate a chunk within the trained span, take its last few frames, condition the next chunk on that tail, and repeat, each chunk conditions on the TAIL of the previous, exactly like a language model continuing its own text. An overlap node such as ImageBatchExtendWithOverlap stitches the seams so motion and lighting carry across. It is enabled by a causal 3D VAE (sliding-window decode), local temporal attention over recent frames, and RoPE's relative-position dot product. It still drifts because each chunk sees only a short tail with no global memory, so error accumulates across segments.

concepts.name: Sliding-Window Extension
concepts.summary: The classic, weaker length-extension method: slide a window of overlapping clips and average where they overlap. Documented failure mode, fine over static backgrounds, but where the background itself moves, latent-space averaging in the overlap regions smears motion into BLUR and inconsistency, a likely reason motion-heavy long Wan videos degrade worst. Contrast with autoregressive chunking, which conditions each chunk on the previous tail instead of averaging overlaps. A related approach is fine-tuned continuation models trained to extend from a few initial frames.
